text:
Rina: heads-up 1: saw a weird microburst in paid-social attribution for yesterday's webinar traffic. conversions up but attributed source moved from organic->paid for a big slice. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/marketing/webinar-topline :eyes:

Carlos: I noticed that too. the UTM_source field on a lot of signups is `null` but the dashboard maps them to paid via last-touch cookie. could be our UTM parsing job.

Priya: quick check: did we change the tracking template for the webinar campaign? I swapped in a new shortlink last week.

Drew: yeah i rolled the shortlink Monday to vanity.link/rw-webinar. it attaches ?utm_campaign=rw-q1 but I didn't include utm_source intentionally since we rely on referrer.

Maya: ok that explains some. still want to validate: referrer detection was updated in the dashboard (sampling flag on) last deploy?

KPI-Bot: alert: webinar_attended_rate anomaly (z=4.2) on 2026-03-03 16:18 UTC for EMEA + APAC cohorts.

Carlos: running a quick comparison between raw_signups and attributed_channels for 03-02..03-03

```
SELECT day, attributed_channel, count(*) as n
FROM analytics.signups
WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-03-02' AND '2026-03-03'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY day, n DESC;
```

Priya: FYI i pulled session_referrer samples and about 18% of the sessions have blank referrer + no UTM_source but do have a utm_campaign value. looks like shortlink lost the source.

Drew: my bad on the shortlink. it rewrites referrers in some mobile clients and strips query params. didn't catch that in local QA.

Rina: impact estimate? if those migrate from organic->paid we've inflated paid conversion for webinar and depressed organic channel in the weekly KPI dashboard.

Carlos: preliminary calc: ~1.7k signups affected across both days, ~12% of yesterday's webinar registrants. that'd shift paid CPL down artificially and organic down by ~9% in the table.

Maya: cool, actionable steps: 1) Priya can we tag the affected rows via event flag (tracking_source="shortlink-v1") so we can reassign in attribution? 2) Drew revert shortlink and regenerate links with utm_source=paid_social? 3) Carlos update dashboard with an alternate attribution rule for the KPI review snapshot (use utm_campaign>utm_source fallback). can we have a patched snapshot before EOD?

Priya: will add the flag at ingestion for rows where utm_campaign exists but utm_source is null and referrer is blank. ETA 2 hours.

Drew: rolling back shortlink now. deploying a fix to preserve querystring on mobile redirect. ETA 30m. apologies. :grimacing:

Carlos: I can build an ad-hoc dashboard slice that applies 'tracking_source' override and post the before/after counts. will also include impact on CPL and MQL rate.

KPI-Bot: note added to weekly_kpi_review (2026-03-05): potential attribution skew from shortlink mobile redirect. reference: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/notes/3069991110-note

Maya: thanks. great triage. please include recommended mitigations and whether we should re-run last week's closed-loop MQL check in Friday notes. we'll discuss at the weekly KPI review. :calendar:

Priya: flagged affected rows and pushed an example CSV to /shared/marketing/shortlink-attr-sample/2026-03-03.csv

Carlos: snapshot posted: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/perf/webinar-shortlink-impact (shows channel_shift and cpl_delta). rough recovery if we reassign flagged rows to organic -> organic MQL rate +8%

Drew: reverted link and deployed fix. will monitor incoming signups for the next 4 hours.

Maya: perfect. this is a good note for the weekly doc. closing thread unless anything else pops up. :lock:

KPI-Bot: summary (auto): 1) root cause: shortlink mobile redirect stripped utm_source; 2) impact: ~12% registrant attribution shift to paid; 3) mitigation: flag and reassign, revert shortlink, regenerate links. archived in /shared/marketing/kpi-incidents/3069991110.json

Carlos: added to Friday's deck under 'Attribution caveats' with recommended wording. end.
